name: Introduction to Qualitative & Quantitative Research Methods
description: There is a growing demand for insights derived from social scientific research among governmental and commercial organisations around the world. Regardless of one’s choice of career, developing skills necessary to understand and evaluate quantitative and qualitative research is essential for us as informed citizens and consumers, so that we can better understand user (individual, group, community) behaviour and preferences towards changes and/or technology advancements that draw on the findings of such research studies. Furthermore, having the knowledge and skills to conduct and oversee research projects is critical in some careers, especially in consulting, policy, data science, product and software design, and for those who want to pursue postgraduate studies. This course introduces students to the fundamentals of qualitative & quantitative social science research, including its epistemological assumptions, and the basics of data collection and analysis. Some questions we will tackle include: What is social science research? What kinds of questions can we ask? What makes good survey and experimental research? How can different approaches offer answers or directions to the questions asked? This course does not require an in-depth understanding of statistics, although some basic knowledge of statistical principles and concepts relevant to social science research is preferred. Participants who take this course will be expected to complete social science research projects to enrich their learning experience by being able to apply the material to real-world problems.
